subject: Exec signoff needed: 5yr price corridor & renewal protections — BridgePath
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Eliot Barnes <eliot@bridgepath.com>, procurement@bridgepath.com, Lara Chen <lara.chen@bridgepath.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec signoff needed: 5yr price corridor & renewal protections — BridgePath

Team —

Quick summary: BridgePath (healthcare analytics) is asking for a 5-year committed contract with a price lock corridor and a limited annual uplift. They are committing to a minimum monthly committed tokens equivalent to ~$120k ARR year 1, with step-ups in years 2–5 tied to usage adoption. This is strategic (pilot across three major customers) and expected to drive ~30% YoY usage growth.

Key commercial asks from BridgePath:
- 5-year price lock on the agreed SKU prices (no general price increases inside the corridor)
- Annual uplift cap: up to 3% compounded (we suggested 2.5%, they countered at 3%)
- Renewal protection: first renewal guaranteed at same corridor pricing provided usage >= 85% of committed baseline; otherwise standard renewal terms apply
- Early-exit: 6-month notice and a ramp-down schedule with a termination fee tied to remaining committed run-rate

Why we should approve:
- Large reference customer in healthcare vertical; strong cross-sell potential into provider contracts
- Predictable committed revenue over 5 years improves utilization planning for Dedicated capacity
- Legal has reviewed and flagged no material IP/data issues for this structure (pending final SOW sign-off)

What I'm asking for:
1) Exec approval to grant the above pricing corridor and the 3% annual uplift cap (exception to our standard 12-month pricing term).
2) Acceptance of the proposed renewal protection language (first renewal protection tied to 85% usage).
3) Permission to allow a fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) as an operational fallback if capacity constraints arise, with explicit mention in the SOW.

Attachments: BridgePath_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood_5yr_price_table.xlsx, Draft_Term_Sheet_BridgePath.docx

If you can sign off with any conditions, please reply — we need to get this into DocuSign for their legal by end of next week (BridgePath is eager to close).

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Eliot Barnes <eliot@bridgepath.com>, procurement@bridgepath.com
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec signoff needed: 5yr price corridor & renewal protections — BridgePath

On Fri, 22 Jun 2028 at 09:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> Quick summary: BridgePath (healthcare analytics)...

Thanks Kim — high level: happy to support but a couple of asks before I can greenlight from RevOps:

1) Uplift calculation: confirm whether the 3% is applied to list price or to the effective committed rate (we should apply to effective committed rate). If applied to list price that increases our effective discount over time.
2) Renewal protection trigger: suggest changing the threshold language to ">= 85% of committed baseline averaged over the 90 days preceding renewal" — makes it less spike-sensitive.
3) Need a short fallback pricing schedule in the SOW that shows stepdown pricing if usage drops below 50% for two consecutive quarters. This helps Finance model downside exposure.

Once the above are clarified and reflected in the draft term sheet, I can approve the corridor and uplift cap as an exception to standard policy.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Eliot Barnes <eliot@bridgepath.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@bridgepath.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec signoff needed: 5yr price corridor & renewal protections — BridgePath

+1 to Marissa's asks. A couple of operational notes from Sales:
- We should include a clear usage remediation path (quarterly business reviews + a 90-day cure period) rather than an immediate stepdown on a single miss.
- Requesting approval for a one-time onboarding credit of $25k (applied in Q1) to cover integration/implementation costs — treats as non-recurring and not part of committed run-rate for uplift calculations.

If we can land the uplift on effective committed rate and adopt Marissa's 90-day averaging for renewal protection, I'm OK to push this through. I'll prepare a short cover memo for Vivek that summarizes revenue and risk impact for approval.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Eliot Barnes <eliot@bridgepath.com>, procurement@bridgepath.com, Lara Chen <lara.chen@bridgepath.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jun 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec signoff needed: 5yr price corridor & renewal protections — BridgePath

Thanks team — reviewed. Approve with the following conditions: 

1) Uplift calculation must be applied to the effective committed rate, not to list price.
2) Renewal protection threshold to be averaged over the 90 days prior to renewal (Marissa's language).
3) Add a 90-day cure period and quarterly business reviews before any stepdown pricing is invoked.
4) Onboarding credit of $25k is approved as one-time, non-recurring.
5) Legal to finalize SOW and confirm fallback model variant language; no DocuSign until Legal signs off.

Kimberly — please update the draft term sheet and SOW to reflect the above items and circulate to Legal. Once legal confirms, Marissa can finalize the RevOps signoff and I will sign the exec approval in DocuSign (send the packet to me at vivek@redwood.com).

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer (acting)
Redwood Inference
